methods.name: validate
methods.description: Check the definition in full, analyse it as a graph, and report every problem with its path

definition.description: The factory definition: its stages, transitions, gates and prompts. Start from one of the skill's examples.

tracker.description: The tracker instance work items publish to, e.g. board: a model of the type the definition's tracker kind needs (the built-in tracker, @swamp/stagecraft/tracker, unless it names another)

scenarios.description: Saved scenarios: work items walked through the definition, which validate runs

methods.name: serve
methods.description: Serve the studio page on 127.0.0.1 until Ctrl-C, and at publicOrigin through a proxy when given: every factory's definition and scenarios, read-only, reloaded as they change; with server, a remote swamp serve's factories instead

port.description: The port on 127.0.0.1; 0, the default, picks a free one

publicOrigin.description: The origin a reverse proxy or tunnel publishes the studio at, such as https://studio.example.com. Requests with that Host or Origin are answered too; the studio has no authentication, so the proxy must provide it

basePath.description: The path a reverse proxy publishes the studio under, such as /_stagecraft. The page's files, API calls and addresses carry it, and requests are answered with or without it, so the proxy may strip it or pass it through. Leave it out to serve at /

server.description: A swamp serve to read instead of this repo, such as wss://swamp.example.com: its factories and work items, read-only, with your own swamp login, refreshed every few seconds. Not with publicOrigin

methods.name: describe
methods.description: Record what this tracker says of itself (its name, contract version, capabilities and the user publish assigns), so a factory can bind to it

methods.name: operate
methods.description: Make one tracker operation and write its answer (the result, or the failure) as a record under the given name; an answer already there that succeeded is kept and nothing is made again

operation.description: The operation: fetch_issue, create, comment, set_status, ...

request.description: The operation's request: an object, or a JSON object as a string

answer.description: The record to write the answer under (answer-...)

run.description: The run asking, recorded with the answer

methods.name: create
methods.description: File a new ticket, numbered by the tracker or under an id you choose

body.description: The new ticket's description, as markdown

type.description: The new ticket's type, from the tracker's own types

id.description: An id of your choosing, such as one that matches a ticket elsewhere (SREMON-2131): shown as written, and lowercased for the ticket's work item key (sremon-2131). It is a label: the built-in tracker never reads or updates that other ticket. Refused when a ticket or work item already has it, or it is this tracker's own <prefix>-<n> form. Absent, the tracker numbers the ticket

methods.name: fetch_issue
methods.description: Fetch a ticket by stable id or display identifier and record a snapshot, with the externalRefs to start a work item from it

issue.description: The ticket: its stable id, or its display identifier

methods.name: claim
methods.description: Start from a ticket: report its work item, or reserve a key for a new one (recorded before it starts) and print the start command

issue.description: The ticket: its stable id, or its display identifier

factory.description: The factory to start a new work item under; needed only when the ticket has no work item, or its last one has finished

dryRun.description: Report the ticket's work item, or that it has none, and write nothing

methods.name: comment
methods.description: Comment on a ticket; with a delivery key, a repeat of the same key posts nothing

workItem.description: The work item this write is for; with journalVersion, makes it idempotent

journalVersion.description: The length of the work item's journal this write reflects

methods.name: set_status
methods.description: Move a ticket to a mapped status (publish is the single writer of a work item's status); already there writes nothing

status.description: A status key, mapped to the tracker's status name by the statuses global argument

workItem.description: The work item this write is for; with journalVersion, makes it idempotent

journalVersion.description: The length of the work item's journal this write reflects

methods.name: relate
methods.description: Relate one ticket to another (parent_of, blocked_by, related_to, duplicate_of) under the rules every tracker shares; already related writes nothing

issue.description: The relation's subject, by stable id: the parent, the blocked ticket, or the duplicate

to.description: The other ticket's stable id: the child, the blocker, or the canonical

workItem.description: The work item this write is for; with journalVersion, makes it idempotent

journalVersion.description: The length of the work item's journal this write reflects

methods.name: mark_duplicate
methods.description: Mark a ticket a duplicate of a primary: relate it duplicate_of and close it where the tracker does not; it moves no work item, and publish and claim refuse the duplicate until a driver moves its work

issue.description: The duplicate: its stable id, or its display identifier

primary.description: The primary it duplicates: its stable id, or its display identifier

workItem.description: The work item this write is for; with journalVersion, makes it idempotent

journalVersion.description: The length of the work item's journal this write reflects

methods.name: unrelate
methods.description: Remove a relation between two tickets; already absent writes nothing

issue.description: The relation's subject, by stable id: the parent, the blocked ticket, or the duplicate

to.description: The other ticket's stable id: the child, the blocker, or the canonical

workItem.description: The work item this write is for; with journalVersion, makes it idempotent

journalVersion.description: The length of the work item's journal this write reflects

methods.name: publish
methods.description: Replay a work item's journal to its ticket: a comment per event a person needs, and the status when the stage's key changes; a re-run delivers only what is new

workItem.description: The work item's name (its key); its externalRefs name the ticket

methods.name: round
methods.description: One round of a run (publish, mark_duplicate, claim, create, fetch_issue), as the shipped workflows drive it: record the answers the tracker's operate wrote for the last round and plan the next

kind.description: What the run does: publish a work item, mark a duplicate, claim a ticket, create one, or fetch one

run.description: The run's id (a workflow's run.id): a new run starts afresh

issue.description: mark_duplicate: the duplicate ticket; claim, fetch_issue: the ticket

factory.description: claim: the factory to start a new work item under

dryRun.description: claim: report the ticket's work item, and write nothing

statusNames.description: conformance: two status names the tracker has, comma-separated; a new ticket starts in neither

missing.description: conformance: a well-formed stable id of no ticket

entryStatus.description: conformance, for a tracker that keeps history: a status name entries may carry

entryTypes.description: conformance, for a tracker that keeps history: two ticket types, comma-separated; a new ticket is in neither

user.description: conformance, for a tracker that assigns: a user it accepts

check.description: Only check that the run finished, and fail if it did not

methods.name: set_type
methods.description: Set a ticket's type (publish is the single writer of a work item's type); already that type writes nothing

workItem.description: The work item this write is for; with journalVersion, makes it idempotent

journalVersion.description: The length of the work item's journal this write reflects

prefix.description: Leads every ticket id and work-item key: lowercase letters, digits and '-', at most 12 characters, e.g. blog for blog-12 (a trailing '-' is dropped). Defaults to the tracker instance's name, cut to 12

statuses.description: The status keys, which are also the status names: a list, or a JSON list as a string. A new ticket starts in the first, and a ticket may move between any two. Defaults to open, in_progress, shipped, closed

types.description: The ticket types: a list, or a JSON list as a string. Defaults to bug, feature, security
